chose: one CSS @custom-variant 'touch' = @media (pointer: coarse), (max-width: 767px), used for every tap-target rule
over: a JS useIsMobile() branch in each primitive
because: AGENTS.md prefers native CSS over JS listeners, and 767px is exactly useIsMobile()'s breakpoint so CSS and JS never disagree about which layout is on screen; pointer-coarse alone misses the narrow desktop window the sidebar already treats as mobile

chose: dropdown-menu goes bottom-sheet on coarse pointers by !important-overriding Base UI's inline positioner styles (position/top/bottom/transform)
over: rendering a real Sheet component instead of Menu.Positioner+Popup
feeding Menu.Positioner a virtual bottom-of-viewport anchor
because: Menu.Item needs to stay inside Menu.Positioner>Menu.Popup for Base UI's composite list and typeahead; the positioner only ever writes position/top/left/transform inline (internals/useAnchorPositioning.js floatingStyles), so a handful of important utilities is the smallest thing that survives its re-renders

chose: no new grocery overflow menu — wired the coarse-pointer sheet into dropdown-menu.tsx only
over: building the 'List actions' menu the design mock shows on the shopping list
because: grep -rl DropdownMenuContent services/web/src == 3 call sites (UserMenu, RandomizerFilterBar, routes/household.list.tsx) and none is the grocery list; the mock illustrates the primitive, and the design's own audit table lists only dropdown-menu.tsx as the work

chose: interactive-badge 44px floor written as touch:[&:is(a,button)]:min-h-(--control-h-touch) on badgeVariants
over: a dedicated size or prop for link badges
because: measured: zero anchor badges and exactly one button badge in services/web (components/collections/CollectionChips.tsx:110, size=xs = 24px); one class with no API beats a mechanism with one subject

chose: left the collections components' existing hand-rolled touch sizing (pointer-coarse:min-h-11, size-11, h-11) in place
over: rewriting them onto the shared control scale
because: CollectionRow/CollectionsSheet/QuickAddRow/AddRecipesSheet/CollectionCheckRow/FileRecipeSheet already render >=44px on a coarse pointer; converting them changes no pixels and only risks regressions

chose: GroceryRow actions stay size=icon-lg (48px on touch), not pinned to exactly 44px
over: forcing 44px to match the floor token exactly
because: 44px is a floor, not a target; hand-pinning a height contradicts the new token comment 'never set a height on a control by hand; pick a size'. Supersedes the earlier pin-to-44px intent

chose: household.index page-wrap mobile padding uses sm: breakpoint, not the touch variant
because: user asked for standard breakpoints here: this is layout density, not a tap-target floor, so it keys off width alone. Also dropped the mobile px-4 that double-padded page-wrap's own calc(100% - 2rem) gutter

chose: plan toolbar wraps to two lines on a phone instead of keeping 28px controls on one line
over: shaving title, gaps and padding to force one row
because: measured 403px of content against 366px of usable width at 390px viewport; three 44px targets + title + date range cannot fit, and the tap-target floor outranks the one-line promise. max-md:h-7/max-md:size-7 were also outranking the shared control scale, which is why those two buttons stayed 28px on mobile

chose: plan toolbar title takes the full row on mobile; controls share the next row
over: letting flex-wrap drop the panel toggle onto its own line
because: measured at 390px: title 366 + controls 244/44 fit two clean rows (bar 92px) instead of a ragged 118px break. 44px floor made the one-line row impossible

chose: collections tree sizes off the app-wide touch: variant, not pointer-coarse:
over: keeping pointer-coarse: so a phone-width desktop window kept 30px rows
because: the tree's only <md surface is CollectionsSheet, so a narrow fine-pointer window showed the sheet with 30px rows and a hover-only gear while every other nav row in the app was 52px. touch: = coarse OR <768, matching useIsMobile
